title: Understanding SVD Output Dimensions
text: When performing Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) on a matrix, the dimensions of the resulting matrices are determined by the dimensions of the original matrix. Consider the shape of the original matrix and how SVD decomposes it.

title: Matrix X Dimensions
text: The matrix X is obtained by subtracting the mean of F from F itself. This operation does not change the number of rows or columns of F. What are the dimensions of X?

title: SVD Decomposition
text: The SVD of a matrix X with dimensions (m,n) results in three matrices: U, S, and Vt. U has dimensions (m,m), S is a diagonal matrix with dimensions (m,n), and Vt has dimensions (n,n). However, when $$full_{matrices}=False$$, the dimensions of U and Vt are reduced. How does this affect their dimensions?

title: Calculate the Dimensions of U and S
text: Given that X has dimensions $$(940,7)$$, and $$full_{matrices}=False$$, what are the dimensions of U and S?

title: Determine the Shape of the Product
text: Now that you know the dimensions of U and S, calculate the shape of the product (U @ np.diag(S)).
